source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check if any mechanical problems occur during installing the MiniDP cable in MiniDP port.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. Make sure the cable can plug/unplug without any problem.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- MiniDP port mechanical check: MiniDP port mechanical check is a physical inspection of the connector seating/strain; human-only.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: operator inspects the MiniDP port + records; agent cannot inspect hardware.

historical_reviews.deepseek: NO; correctly recognizes the physical inspection, but provides no connector-damage or active-console boundary.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY / IMPROVED; adds cable identity, fit/force/retention criteria, ESD, stop conditions and recovery.

original_test_intent: Verify that the specified Mini DisplayPort cable can be inserted into and removed from the intended MiniDP connector with normal alignment, seating, retention and no mechanical damage.
original_method: A qualified operator inspects the connector and approved cable, performs one controlled mate/unmate cycle by hand, assesses force, seating and retention, and captures before/after photographs.
manual_activity: Insertion/removal force, alignment, latch/retention, connector movement and visible damage are tactile/visual facts that an engineer must assess at the chassis.
required_inputs: Exact MiniDP connector and approved cable/adapter part number
Allowed insertion/removal direction, retention and damage criteria
ESD procedure and active display/console impact
Qualified operator, photo evidence and alternate console
safety_requirements: Do not force a keyed or misaligned connector.
Stop immediately on unusual resistance, wobble, bent contacts, shroud/PCB movement or latch failure.
Do not repeatedly cycle a damaged connector or use an unapproved adapter/tool.
Protect an active console/display path and do not retry automatically after an abnormal fit.
agent_execution_scope: Prepare the connector/cable identity and before/after evidence checklist.
Collect read-only display/driver health before and after if the port was active.
Organize operator observations without claiming tactile or visual execution.
engineer_actions: Approve the cable and mechanical limits.
Inspect and perform one careful mate/unmate cycle under ESD controls.
Assess fit, retention and damage and issue PASS/FAIL.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correct: no software command can measure the required tactile/visual mechanical result.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No replacement command. Display detection may document post-action health but is outside the primary mechanical acceptance.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: MiniDP plug/unplug criterion, photo/log collection and 5/0-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use an approved cable gauge/part, inspect with magnification if available, perform one aligned insertion/removal, record seating and connector movement, and verify any active display path afterward.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact chassis/board MiniDP connector and approved cable assembly.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record board/chassis and cable revisions; software version is not the acceptance basis.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Owner mechanical drawing, connector and cable specifications.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds identity, stop thresholds and pre/post damage evidence without increasing cycle count.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; electrical video quality remains a separate testcase.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Subjective force assessment should not be converted into an invented numeric limit.
modernized_recommendation.recommended_tooling: Camera/magnifier and only owner-approved force gauge if a documented limit exists.

project_override_considerations: A project may define part numbers and quantitative force/retention limits. Missing limits make execution not ready, not permanently blocked. Additional mating cycles require separate authorization because they increase wear.
expected_evidence: SUT/port/cable identities and mechanical acceptance criteria
Timestamped before/after connector and cable photographs
Operator observation of alignment, force, seating, retention and absence of damage
Restored display/console state, unexpected-log review and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The procedure and criterion consistently require a physical MiniDP fit/unfit inspection.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The manual action is clear. Cable identity and acceptance limits are readiness inputs rather than permanent blockers.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Agree with human-only classification but add physical-damage and service boundaries.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agree with MANUAL ONLY and retain its one-cycle, ESD and stop-condition safeguards.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates mechanical fit coverage from optional electrical display evidence and prohibits unsupported repeated cycling.

review_improvement: Turns 'without any problem' into bounded, reviewable fit evidence without inventing force limits or risking repeated connector damage.
independent_technical_reasoning: The acceptance signal is tactile and visual at the connector. Neither OS enumeration nor video output can establish insertion force or physical damage, so the case is MANUAL ONLY.
